subject: Post-demo decision memo: model lanes, perf anchors, and next-step checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@asterlabs.com>, Priya Kulkarni <pkulkarni@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo decision memo: model lanes, perf anchors, and next-step checklist

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and clear priorities. Summarizing call outcomes and proposing a tight pilot plan so we can get you meaningful perf and quality data quickly. High-level notes: 

- Business need: ~20–50 QPS peak for customer-facing summarization with strict 200ms median latency target for the interactive UI. Occasional batch re-runs for analytics.
- Primary risk: hallucination on domain-specific entities (medical device IDs). Needs regression hooks and guardrails.
- Success signals: p95 latency < 400ms, throughput sustained at 20 QPS with tail latency under 1s, per-case hallucination rate < 2% on the supplied audit set.

Recommendation (decision lanes):
1) Default lane — RLHF-medium quantized (4-bit): best balance of cost and quality for demo/pilot (we've validated with Redwood-verified perf profile). Expect ~22 TPS on a 4xA100 pool, p50 ~140ms, p95 ~390ms for 512-token sequences.
2) Low-latency lane — distilled-small (optimized kernels): for interactive hotspots; target p50 < 80ms, p95 < 240ms but slightly lower recall on rare entities.
3) High-accuracy lane — rlhf-large (fp16): for batch analytics and validation steps; higher cost, better handling of rare tokens.

I've attached a short packet with the perf profiles (redwood_perf_profiles_20270901.pdf) and a prompt pack we recommend we run during the pilot (pilot_prompt_pack_v2.zip). Live benchmark traces from our compatibility run with a sample of your data are in benchmark-traces-aster-20270825.tar.gz. Links to online artifacts are below.

Next steps I propose (please confirm owners & timing):
- Aster: confirm pilot scope (sample size, top-100 queries & labels) and procurement timeline (target start week of Sep 13).
- Redwood: run a focused throughput/latency sweep for the three lanes on your sample within 5 business days of receiving the sample.
- Security/compliance: Priya — please forward any SSF/SOC 2 questions; we will pull evidence.

If this alignment looks good I'll assign Marissa to run the pilot and Aditya to own perf tuning and KV-cache config.

Short ask: Can you confirm the pilot data export by end of day Friday (Sep 3)? That will let us hit a Sep 14 pilot kickoff.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Solutions Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: redwood_perf_profiles_20270901.pdf (model lanes + TPS/latency percentiles), pilot_prompt_pack_v2.zip (prompt templates + regression checks), benchmark-traces-aster-20270825.tar.gz (raw traces)
From: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@asterlabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kulkarni <pkulkarni@asterlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo decision memo: model lanes, perf anchors, and next-step checklist

Hi Naomi — appreciate the clear write-up. Quick answers:

- Pilot scope: we'll start with our Top-10k customer-facing summaries (sampled) + 500 labeled cases for hallucination checks.
- Timeline: procurement is tight but doable; we can aim for Sep 14 kickoff as long as we get the pricing and contract terms by next Tuesday (Sep 7).
- Security: Priya will send over the security questionnaire this afternoon (SOC 2 + data residency questions).

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm estimated cost range for the 3 model lanes for a 30-day pilot (ballpark USD)?
2) Are the prompt sets editable during the pilot, and can we run A/B variants?

Thanks — Sanjeev
Sanjeev Rao | Head of ML Platforms | Aster Labs
sanjeev@asterlabs.com | +1 617-555-7834
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Priya Kulkarni <pkulkarni@asterlabs.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo decision memo: model lanes, perf anchors, and next-step checklist

Thanks Sanjeev — quick answers below and an explicit action list.

Cost estimate (ballpark for 30-day pilot with 10k daily avg queries, 3 lanes active but low-usage for high-accuracy lane):
- Default lane (rlhf-medium quantized): ~$6k–9k (compute + hosting)
- Low-latency lane (distilled-small): ~$2k–3k
- High-accuracy lane (rlhf-large fp16 for batch): ~$8k–12k (on-demand bursts)
Total range: ~$16k–24k depending on hit rates and sequence lengths. We'll create a more granular cost table once you share the sample token distribution.

Prompt sets: fully editable during the pilot. Recommend we run two variants (A/B) as part of the regression checklist; pilot_prompt_pack_v2.zip includes suggested A/B splits and evaluation harness.

Security questionnaire: Priya — we've attached the standard SOC2 evidence pack link; if you need an encrypted artifact or on-prem proofs we can discuss.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Aster: share sample export (Top-10k sampling + 500 labeled cases) — owner: Priya — ETA: EOD Sep 3.
- Redwood: run perf sweep on sample across three lanes and return a perf-pad with TPS/p50/p95 traces — owner: Marissa — ETA: Sep 10.
- Redwood: produce a cost sensitivity table after token distribution received — owner: Aditya — ETA: Sep 10.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync next week to walk through the perf-pad and pick the default lane. Marissa — can you take the pilot engineering lead (I added you to thread)?

Best,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Post-demo decision memo: model lanes, perf anchors, and next-step checklist

Looping in quick ops notes and pilot checklist. I'll own the perf sweep and run the three lanes on a mirrored infra. Preliminary runbook: 

- Day 0 (prep): confirm token distribution and sample format; get access to S3 export (read-only).
- Day 1–3: run 3x A100 runs for the default lane to capture sustained TPS and p95; collect KV-cache hit profiles.
- Day 4: run low-latency distill configuration with kernel tuning; report p50/p95.
- Day 5: batch-run rlhf-large for the labeled set and compute hallucination metrics.

Regression guardrails we'll instrument during the sweep: prompt-degradation detector (baseline perplexity drift), hallucination classifier on labeled cases, and a nightly regression alert if hallucination rate increases >0.5% from baseline.

I also confirmed the attachments Naomi referenced are staged in our internal drive (link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/AST-PILOT-REQS-2027). Sanjeev/Priya — once you share the export I'll create a short run-schedule and calendar invites for kickoff.

- Marissa
